title: The Things I See
content: I go there every night, it’s been so consistent, over so many years; I’ve really begun to wonder if I’m not living some sort of double life. These are some of the landmarks and paths I take for comparison (to yours). A long, winding, dirt road that leads from fields, and forest, to an interstate filled with traffic. It bridges across to the city that seems to always be under construction. The bridge is reminiscent of the 7 Mile Bridge in Florida. One of the few times someone interacted with me, they were driving the car, and crashed it off the bridge. I swam to safety but, it’s effected me in reality. Just before the bridge there’s a gas station/deli/cafe. I stop in and check out the flavors of the day. The shopping center is like if Mall of America was set up like a strip mall vs multiple floors. There’s walls of glass but, no amusement park. There’s toys, clothes, an electronics department; the works. I tend to trip, find boxes a lot; as though an employee didn’t finish putting things out. People move past me, and sometimes cause anxiety but, they don’t really interact, just stare. I’ll go up and down the fresh produce and pick out things for lunch. However leaving the store is always a pain. If I try to go out the front, the store will be closing, and there’s long lines at the registers as people try to hustle out the doors. When I finally get outside, it’s night, and the parking lot is empty except a few cars. I feel like I’ve been left behind. *If I leave through the mall*, the “day” continues, and I find myself window shopping downtown. Downtown is where the “library” is with its dim lighting yet infinite seeming shelves. I go there after the oddity shop. Downtown also has a bar, theater, and garage. The houses in the neighborhood are like those of classy New Orleans; the long houses with wrap around porches on both levels. Half is a desert, half is like a park. There’s industrial buildings and the like along the water. There’s a hotel/apartment building also on the waters edge. If you walk around enough you find the doors can lead to the other locations listed. There’s a lake surrounded by pine trees. There’s trails/paths that encircle it. I get there by walking through the woods and avoiding the bridge. If I “camp” in one spot, the weather will change; a lot of times snowing me in. There’s a cave I found recently that overlooks everything. Sometimes that’s how I enter the dream scape. That’s all I can think of. I’ll happily answer questions.
